key_insight: GCcore is a hyperparameter-free, deterministic coreset selection method that uses pathology foundation model embeddings to choose a small, highly representative set of images for annotation.
clinical_relevance: By reducing the amount of expert labeling needed, this approach could help make computational pathology model development and validation more efficient in settings with limited pathologist time.
method: Embed every image with a pathology foundation model
Greedily select samples that maximize global coverage of the embedding space
Provide a lower-bound guarantee on coverage for any coreset size
evidence_signal: Across 10 tasks and datasets spanning whole slide image classification, tile classification, and tissue segmentation, GCcore ranked first on six tasks and in the top three on nine, outperforming 14 baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the choice of foundation model embeddings, so real-world deployment may still require validation across institutions, scanners, and pathology subdomains.
paper_title: Label-Free Coreset Selection with Foundation Models for Efficient Annotation in Computational Pathology
